q: 1. Lime mortar is generally made with ............
explain: Hydraulic lime is preferred for mortar because it has the property of setting under water or in thick walls where air circulation is limited, making it suitable for structural masonry.

q: 2. The commonly used lime in white-washing, is ............
explain: Fat lime (also known as rich lime or white lime) is used for white-washing and plastering because it slakes vigorously, has high plasticity, and provides a smooth, white finish.

q: 3. The initial setting time of lime-pozzolona, is ............
explain: The addition of pozzolana to lime influences the setting properties, but the standard initial setting time for this mix is also categorized at 120 minutes.

q: 4. The commonly used raw material in the manufacture of cement, is ............
explain: Limestone provides the essential calcium carbonate (calcareous component) required for the production of Portland cement.

q: 5. Pick up the compound responsible for early strength of cement from the following ............
explain: Tri-calcium silicate (C3S) hydrates quickly and is responsible for the high early strength of cement within the first 7 days.

q: 6. The expansion in Portland cement can be tested by ............
explain: The soundness test (using Le-Chatelier apparatus) measures the ability of cement to retain its volume and detects expansion caused by free lime.

q: 7. The final setting time of ordinary Portland cement should not be less than ............
explain: The final setting time for OPC should not exceed 10 hours (600 minutes) as per standard engineering specifications.

q: 8. The initial and final setting times of quick setting cement are ............
explain: Quick setting cement has a very short initial setting time (5 minutes) and a final setting time of 30 minutes.

q: 9. If P is the percentage of water required for normal consistency, water to be added for determination of initial setting time, is ............
explain: Standard tests specify using 0.85P water for setting time and soundness (Le-Chatelier) tests.

q: 10. Index number expressing the relative sizes of both coarse and fine aggregates, is called ............
explain: Fineness Modulus (FM) is an empirical factor obtained by adding the cumulative percentages of aggregate retained on each of the standard sieves and dividing the sum by 100.

q: 11. If water required for 1 bag of cement is 30 litres, the water cement ratio is ............
explain: One bag of cement weighs 50 kg. W/C ratio = weight of water / weight of cement = 30 kg / 50 kg = 0.60.

q: 12. The clinker is formed at a temperature of ............
explain: Nodular clinkers are formed in the rotary kiln at sintering temperatures around 1400°C to 1500°C.

q: 13. The compound responsible for the initial setting of cement, is ............
explain: Tri-calcium Aluminate (C3A) reacts most rapidly with water and is primarily responsible for the initial setting and stiffening.But in Answer key Of Book c is the correct option

q: 14. The percentage of the slag component of Portland-slag cement varies from ............
explain: Portland Slag Cement (PSC) is made by mixing cement clinker with blast furnace slag. Commercial ratios typically fall between 40% and 70% slag.

q: 15. The durability of concrete is proportional to
explain: A higher cement-aggregate ratio (more cement relative to aggregate) generally leads to a denser, stronger, and more durable concrete mix.

q: 16. The shrinkage of ordinary concrete is about
explain: The total shrinkage of ordinary cement concrete under standard conditions is approximately 0.0003 to 0.0006 (or 0.3 to 0.6 mm per meter).

q: 17. According to Indian standard specifications, the concrete should be cured under a humidity of
explain: For effective hydration of cement, concrete should be cured in a very moist environment, typically with a relative humidity of 90% or higher.

q: 18. The most commonly used in cement is
explain: Gypsum ($CaSO_4 \cdot 2H_2O$) is added during cement grinding to act as a retarder, preventing flash set and controlling the initial setting time.

q: 19. In the chemical composition test for loss on ignition, the cement is heated to a temperature of
explain: Loss on ignition is determined by heating the cement sample to 900-1000°C to ensure all organic matter and moisture are expelled.

q: 20. Excessive free lime and excessive magnesia present in the cement make the cement
options: to have very low initial setting time
to have very low compressive strength
explain: Free lime ($CaO$) and magnesia ($MgO$) undergo slow hydration and expansion after the cement has set, leading to cracking, known as unsoundness.

q: 21. Snowcem is
explain: Snowcem is a well-known commercial brand of waterproof cement paint, essentially composed of white or colored Portland cement.

q: 22. The variety of pig iron used for the manufacture of steel by Bessemer process, is
explain: The Bessemer process specifically requires Bessemer pig iron, which is low in phosphorus and silicon.

q: 23. Hydraulic lime is obtained by ...............
explain: Kankar is an impure form of limestone containing clay. When burnt, the silica and alumina in the clay react to give the lime its hydraulic properties (ability to set under water).

q: 24. The process of manufacturing steel by heating short lengths of wrought iron bars mixed with charcoal in the clay crucibles... is known as
explain: The crucible process involves melting wrought iron and charcoal in a closed vessel to produce high-quality, uniform cast steel.

q: 25. For high grade instruments the steel preferred to, is ...............
explain: Cast Steel: High-carbon steel made in crucibles is hard, uniform, and suitable for high-grade, high-hardness tools and instruments.

q: 26. The fluxing agent in the manufacturing of white cement is ...............
explain: Cryolite is used as a flux in white cement to lower the fusion temperature without adding color-forming oxides like iron.

q: 27. Minimum required water cement ratio for a workable concrete is ...............
explain: While 0.23 to 0.25 is enough for chemical hydration, at least 0.38 to 0.40 is required to provide workability in practical construction conditions.

q: 28. The lime which contains high percentage of calcium oxide, is generally called ...............
explain: Fat lime (also known as high-calcium or pure lime) contains more than 93% Calcium Oxide. It slakes vigorously and increases in volume significantly.

q: 29. Most economical of the methods of sawing wood is ...............
explain: Flat sawing (or plain sawing) involves making parallel cuts through the log. It is the fastest and least wasteful method, though it may produce more warping.

q: 30. A thin sheet of wood sliced from a log of wood is called ...............
explain: Veneers are thin slices of wood, usually less than 3mm thick, which are glued onto core panels to produce plywood or decorative surfaces.

q: 31. The rapid hardening Portland cement is obtained by ...............
options: grinding the clinker to a high degree of fineness
adding calcium sulphate to the mixture
burning the mixture at a lower temperature
explain: Increased fineness allows for a larger surface area for hydration, which accelerates the strength development in the early stages.

q: 32. Le-chatelier method is used to determine ...............
explain: The Le-Chatelier test measures the expansion of cement paste due to 'unsound' free lime, ensuring the concrete won't crack after setting.
Gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O) is an evaporite mineral, formed by the chemical precipitation of calcium sulphate from evaporating seawater.

q: 34. The defect caused due to over-maturity and unventilated storage of the wood during its transit is called ..........
explain: Foxiness is indicated by yellow or red stains in wood caused by poor ventilation or decay due to over-maturity.

q: 35. Pozzolana (or surkhi) is used in lime .............
options: to decrease the cost of construction
explain: Pozzolana reacts with the calcium hydroxide in lime to form compounds with cementitious properties, effectively imparting hydraulic properties to non-hydraulic lime.

q: 36. Slump test facilitates .............
options: controlling of water-cement ratio of concrete during construction
the determination of initial and final setting times of cement
the determination of workability of concrete
explain: As Per Book Key A. The slump test is a simple field test used to measure the consistency or workability of a fresh concrete mix.

q: 37. The coefficient of linear expansion of concrete is ............
options: almost same as that of steel
many times more than that of steel
explain: Concrete and steel have very similar thermal expansion coefficients ($12 	imes 10^{-6}/°C$), which prevents structural failure during temperature changes in Reinforced Cement Concrete.

q: 38. Eminently hydraulic lime is one in which the percentage of silica, alumina and iron oxide is ......
explain: Eminently hydraulic lime contains 25-30% clayey impurities, allowing it to set under water in 1-2 days.

q: 39. The commonly used lime for works under water or in damp situation is ............
explain: Eminently hydraulic lime is used for underwater structures because it hardens through chemical reaction with water, not air.

q: 40. The constituent in lime which retard the slaking action and increase the rapidity of setting, is ...
explain: The constituent in lime which retards the slaking action and increases the rapidity of setting is silica.

q: 41. Which of the following timbers is suitable for making sports goods?
explain: Mulberry is flexible and tough, making it the ideal choice for hockey sticks, tennis rackets, and cricket bats.

q: 42. The ingredient which accounts for the most in cement is ............
explain: Lime (Calcium Oxide) constitutes about 60% to 67% of Portland cement.

q: 43. The rocks which are formed due to cooling of magma at a relatively shallow depth from the earth surface are called ............
explain: Hypabyssal rocks (like dolerite) form at shallow depths, showing crystal sizes intermediate between plutonic and volcanic rocks.

q: 44. The bulking of sand is due to ............
options: the increase in space between the particles caused by the surface tension effect of moisture
the swelling of air in voids
explain: Bulking of sand occurs when moisture forms a thin film around sand particles, and surface tension pushes the particles apart, increasing the overall volume.

q: 45. Rapid hardening cement attains early strength due to ............
options: larger proportion of lime grounded finer than normal cement
lesser proportion of lime grounded coarser than normal cement
lesser proportion of lime grounded finer than normal cement
larger proportion of lime grounded coarser than normal cement
explain: Higher lime content and finer grinding increase the surface area for hydration, allowing the cement to gain strength much faster than OPC.

q: 46. The most common admixture which is used to accelerate the initial set of concrete is ............
explain: Calcium chloride is the most widely used accelerator to speed up the setting and early strength development of concrete.
